lead_title: Henry Nowak ‘would have hated’ riots after his murder, says family

evidence_pages.https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026:
Henry Nowak ‘would have hated’ riots after his murder, says family | Crime | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Mark Nowak with his son, Henry, who was murdered by Vickrum Digwa in December 2025.Photograph: Family handout/PAView image in fullscreenMark Nowak with his son, Henry, who was murdered by Vickrum Digwa in December 2025.Photograph: Family handout/PA
Henry Nowak ‘would have hated’ riots after his murder, says family
Parents of teenager stabbed in Southampton last year hit out at political ‘game’ played with son’s murder
Henry Nowak’s family said he “would have hated” the riots that followed his death as they accused some politicians of playing a “game” with their son’s murder.
Nowak, who was fatally stabbed by Vickrum Digwa last year, was handcuffed by police as he lay dying when his attacker falsely accused him of racial abuse.
The Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, subsequently delivered an emergency address calling for the public to respond with “pure cold rage” and demanding an end to what he described as “two-tier policing”.
Protesters – including the leaders of Ukip and Britain First, the Portsmouth branch of the National Rebirth party and others called to attend on social media – demonstrated inSouthamptonin the weeks after Nowak’s death.
Speaking in an interview for an ITV Tonight documentary, Dear Henry: Our Fight for Justice, the family said they had “worked hard” to keep politics out of Nowak’s story.
Nowak’s mother, Lucy Ross, said she thought some people had tried to use her son’s death to advance wider political arguments.
“I suppose that’s the game they play, and I can’t do anything about that. But when they think it all links together – no, it doesn’t,” she said.
“Olivia’s lost her brother, and I’ve lost my son. I’m not interested in your political game.
“I want to know why Henry was on the floor, and he got treated the way he did, but that family got treated [in] a different way. What is that?”
Mark Nowak told ITV that his son “was not a divisive person” and the political response to his murder “didn’t sit with Henry’s values or our values”.
TheIndependent Office for Police Conduct(IOPC) confirmed that its investigation into potential failures in the police response to Nowak’s stabbing is expected to wrap up early next year.
A letter sent to the family by the watchdog in April said that, after “careful consideration of the available evidence”, no officers “would be subject to conduct or criminal investigation”.
It read: “This was because there were no concerns identified in relation to officer actions and decisions that would be so serious as to justify the bringing of disciplinary proceedings, should they be proven or admitted.”
The letter added that the decision not to investigate attending officers would be “kept under review throughout the life cycle of the case”.
The IOPC announced in July that two officers were under investigation for potential gross misconduct.
The home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, has also commissioned an independent review of the case, including the IOPC’s involvement, led by the former lord chancellor Alex Chalk, to examine whether there were “any missed opportunities to intervene”.
Speaking to ITV, she said she had been “very moved by the dignity of the family in how they’ve handled this awful situation which none of us can ever imagine being in, and I’m very clear that they deserve answers and I have committed to them that it’s my job to make sure that they get the answers”.

Henry Nowak family say police failed them multiple times - BBC News
ITV released footage from 'Dear Henry: Our Fight for Justice - A Tonight Special' that airs on Thursday 5 November at 21:00 GMT
The family of murdered student Henry Nowak have said police gave changing accounts of the events surrounding his death and did not initially disclose they had handcuffed him as he lay dying.
They said police initially portrayed him as the aggressor in the fatal altercation with killer Vickrum Digwa in Southampton on 3 December 2025.
The 18-year-old's stepmother Katie Nowak said Hampshire Police had failed them "multiple times".
The remarks came in a second excerpt released by ITVfrom the forthcoming documentary Dear Henry: Our Fight For Justice. Chief Constable Alexis Boon has apologised to the family and said that when Henry "needed us most, we failed him".
Nowak, from Chafford Hundred in Essex, was a first-year student at the University of Southampton when he was murdered as he walked home from a night out.
He suffered five stab wounds or cuts from a 21cm (8in) blade, which Digwa later claimed was from a kirpan that he was carrying as part of his Sikh faith.
Image source,Family photoImage caption,
Henry Nowak, 18, was fatally stabbed in Southampton in December 2025
In police body-worn camera footage that was shown in court, the teenager could be heard repeating, "I've been stabbed", to which an officer replies: "Don't think you have, mate."
The family told ITV News they first saw the footage on the first day of Digwa's trial at Southampton Crown Court.
Henry's sister Olivia said: "That video only came out because there was a trial. We didn't see it before the trial."
Katie Nowak added: "We've always felt that there was a slight hope that Vickrum may have pleaded guilty.
"And if he'd have pleaded guilty or we hadn't have hired expert help, we've always had that fear that the truth may never have come out."
Henry's stepmother Katie Nowak said the family felt "manipulated" by the police
In another excerpt, she said: "I do feel that we have been failed multiple times.
"I fear that we may have been manipulated in our darkest hours.
"I fear that some decisions were made to try and protect the police and their reputation rather than help us as a family."
The teenager's father Mark Nowak said police gave differing accounts of what happened on 3 December.
"The story was evolving every time we had an interaction," he said.
"That evolution of what actually happened that night really shocked us, and we felt we were being hoodwinked. We felt we were being not told the truth."
He also recalled being asked to approve a draft police press release that depicted his son as an aggressor.
The student's sister Olivia Nowak and mother Lucy Ross also spoke to ITV
Hampshire and Isle of Wight Chief Constable Alexis Boon told ITV in a statement: "Henry's murder was a devastating tragedy, and our thoughts remain with his family and all those who loved him.
"I am incredibly sorry that in his final moments, when he needed us most, we failed him.
"For Henry's family, this has been about more than the circumstances of one night.
"They have rightly raised serious concerns about the police response and their treatment throughout the investigation and since. No family should ever find themselves in this position."
The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) confirmed its investigation into potential failures in the police response to Mr Nowak's stabbing is expected to be concluded early next year.
However, a letter sent to the family by the watchdog in April said after "careful consideration of the available evidence" no officers "would be subject to conduct or criminal investigation".
It read: "This was because there were no concerns identified in relation to officer actions and decisions that would be so serious as to justify the bringing of disciplinary proceedings, should they be proven or admitted."
The letter added the decision not to investigate attending officers would be "kept under review throughout the life cycle of the case".
The IOPC announced in July that two officers were under investigation for potential gross misconduct.
IOPC director of engagement Derrick Campbell said the watchdog was "committed to establishing the full circumstances of this case, including whether any of the officers involved should face disciplinary proceedings" and providing Mr Nowak's family with answers.
"We are working hard to conclude our independent investigation as quickly as possible while ensuring we have robustly explored all lines of inquiry," he said.
Campbell added investigators are in "regular contact" with Mr Nowak's family members.
Digwa, 23, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years.
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced an independent inquiry into the murder, led by former lord chancellor Alex Chalk, which will look at "any missed opportunities to intervene".

Clancy’s lawyers urgedJudge William Sullivanon Monday to dismiss the first-degree murder charges against her in the state of Massachusetts in the United States, saying retrying her for killing her three young children would violate ⁠⁠her constitutional rights.

Prosecutors said they intend to retry Clancy if the case moves forward but have not decided if she would face the same first-degree murder charges.
Monday’s hearing was her second time in court since September, when jurors were unable to reacha verdictat her trial.
Clancy strangled her three children with exercise bands in 2023 at her home in Duxbury, a suburb of Boston in Massachusetts. Clancy then attempted to take her own life by cutting herself with a knife and was paralysed after jumping from a second-floor window.
At Monday’s hearing, defence lawyer Martin G Weinberg argued that the judge should have investigated further after the jury foreperson sent two notes indicating that a juror was not following the rules. Further questioning could have revealed grounds to remove the juror, identified as Michael Desronvil, and continue deliberations, he said.
After receiving the notes, Sullivan spoke with each juror, reminding them of their duties and explaining what constitutes reasonable doubt in a court case. He asked whether they could apply the law to the case, and all said yes.
But Weinberg argued that Sullivan had not gone far enough. A juror who said he could follow the law could have been lying, Weinberg said, and the situation warranted questioning the foreperson separately to learn more about what was happening during deliberations.
Assistant District Attorney Jennifer Sprague argued there was no indication the holdout juror’s disagreement stemmed from personal bias or an inability to deliberate, rather than a different assessment of the evidence.
Sprague said the judge handled the ⁠⁠jury impasse appropriately, saying the fact that one juror dug in his heels did not mean Sullivan should risk interfering with the deliberations by questioning him.
“It is clear from the record this ⁠⁠juror did not refuse to deliberate,” Sprague said. “He refused to agree.”
Defence lawyer Kevin Reddington accused the lone holdout juror of using a mobile phone to research terms related to the case and questioned whether he had been truthful during jury selection.
Clancy has never disputed killing her three young children in 2023, but her lawyer has argued she had postpartum psychosis and was unable to control her behaviour. Prosecutors have acknowledged that Clancy, now 36, had mental health problems but said she acted deliberately and understood her actions were wrong.
Sullivan did not immediately rule on the motion to dismiss. He scheduled another hearing for November 16 and suggested a retrial could begin in March.
Another motion expected to be discussed is the state of Massachusetts’s request for a gag order barring lawyers and their supporters “from making extrajudicial statements to the media that would have a substantial likelihood of materially prejudicing the criminal proceeding”.

Henry Nowak ‘would have hated’ riots after his murder, says family
Parents of teenager stabbed in Southampton last year hit out at political ‘game’ played with son’s murder
Henry Nowak’s family said he “would have hated” the riots that followed his death as they accused some politicians of playing a “game” with their son’s murder.
Nowak, who was fatally stabbed by Vickrum Digwa last year, was handcuffed by police as he lay dying when his attacker falsely accused him of racial abuse.

The Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, subsequently delivered an emergency address calling for the public to respond with “pure cold rage” and demanding an end to what he described as “two-tier policing”.

Protesters – including the leaders of Ukip and Britain First, the Portsmouth branch of the National Rebirth party and others called to attend on social media – demonstrated inSouthamptonin the weeks after Nowak’s death.
Speaking in an interview for an ITV Tonight documentary, Dear Henry: Our Fight for Justice, the family said they had “worked hard” to keep politics out of Nowak’s story.
Nowak’s mother, Lucy Ross, said she thought some people had tried to use her son’s death to advance wider political arguments.
“I suppose that’s the game they play, and I can’t do anything about that.
But when they think it all links together – no, it doesn’t,” she said.
“Olivia’s lost her brother, and I’ve lost my son.
“I want to know why Henry was on the floor, and he got treated the way he did, but that family got treated [in] a different way.
Mark Nowak told ITV that his son “was not a divisive person” and the political response to his murder “didn’t sit with Henry’s values or our values”.
TheIndependent Office for Police Conduct(IOPC) confirmed that its investigation into potential failures in the police response to Nowak’s stabbing is expected to wrap up early next year.
A letter sent to the family by the watchdog in April said that, after “careful consideration of the available evidence”, no officers “would be subject to conduct or criminal investigation”.

It read: “This was because there were no concerns identified in relation to officer actions and decisions that would be so serious as to justify the bringing of disciplinary proceedings, should they be proven or admitted.”
The letter added that the decision not to investigate attending officers would be “kept under review throughout the life cycle of the case”.
The IOPC announced in July that two officers were under investigation for potential gross misconduct.

The home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, has also commissioned an independent review of the case, including the IOPC’s involvement, led by the former lord chancellor Alex Chalk, to examine whether there were “any missed opportunities to intervene”.

Speaking to ITV, she said she had been “very moved by the dignity of the family in how they’ve handled this awful situation which none of us can ever imagine being in, and I’m very clear that they deserve answers and I have committed to them that it’s my job to make sure that they get the answers”.

The family of murdered student Henry Nowak have said police gave changing accounts of the events surrounding his death and did not initially disclose they had handcuffed him as he lay dying.
They said police initially portrayed him as the aggressor in the fatal altercation with killer Vickrum Digwa in Southampton on 3 December 2025.
The 18-year-old's stepmother Katie Nowak said Hampshire Police had failed them "multiple times".
The remarks came in a second excerpt released by ITVfrom the forthcoming documentary Dear Henry: Our Fight For Justice.
Chief Constable Alexis Boon has apologised to the family and said that when Henry "needed us most, we failed him".
Nowak, from Chafford Hundred in Essex, was a first-year student at the University of Southampton when he was murdered as he walked home from a night out.
He suffered five stab wounds or cuts from a 21cm (8in) blade, which Digwa later claimed was from a kirpan that he was carrying as part of his Sikh faith.
Henry Nowak, 18, was fatally stabbed in Southampton in December 2025
In police body-worn camera footage that was shown in court, the teenager could be heard repeating, "I've been stabbed", to which an officer replies: "Don't think you have, mate."
The family told ITV News they first saw the footage on the first day of Digwa's trial at Southampton Crown Court.
Henry's sister Olivia said: "That video only came out because there was a trial.
Katie Nowak added: "We've always felt that there was a slight hope that Vickrum may have pleaded guilty.
"And if he'd have pleaded guilty or we hadn't have hired expert help, we've always had that fear that the truth may never have come out."
Henry's stepmother Katie Nowak said the family felt "manipulated" by the police
In another excerpt, she said: "I do feel that we have been failed multiple times.
"I fear that we may have been manipulated in our darkest hours.

ByGavin BlackburnPublished on3 November 2026 - 7:53 GMT+1•Updated8:36ShareCommentsAdd Euronews on GoogleShareFacebookTwitterFlipboardSendRedditLinkedinMessengerTelegramVKBlueskyThreadsWhatsapp
A 2024 United Nations report said proceeds from North Korean cyberattacks had "reportedly helped to fund the country's development of weapons of mass destruction".
Pyongyang has blasted the FBI's allegations that it was behind the theft of $6 billion (€5.3 billion) from cryptocurrency platform Binance, as it test-fired strategic cruise missiles in a new display of its weapons capabilities.
The missile launch came on the heels of a public rebuttal from Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong-un, who slammed the FBI's allegations as a "grave political provocation".
On Saturday, theFBI said a North Korea-affiliated hacking group called TraderTraitorhad been behind the hack.
Experts see the incident as potentially the largest cryptocurrency theft in history, with a haul equalling "nearly a quarter of the DPRK's estimated annual GDP," Michael Bosack, founding director of the Parley Policy Institute and a former UN Command official, told the AFP news agency.
Kim Yo-jong said the FBI's claim was "absurd rhetoric and nothing new," given prior US allegations that Pyongyang was behind last year's major hack of Bybit.
Still, North Korea likely felt compelled to respond because of the "level of international attention on the incident", Bosack said.
A TV screen shows a file image of Kim Yo-jong during a news programme at the Seoul Railway Station in Seoul, 1 June, 2023AP Photo
The denial was aimed at maintaining channels through which North Korea could continue laundering and using the cryptocurrency, Bosack added.
"If external parties start closing doors based on the international heat on the matter, then the stolen cryptocurrency does nothing to support the Kim regime's near-term priorities," he said.
The hack has prompted South Korea to call for increased protections for its digital infrastructure against cyberattacks.
"Not long ago, even the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange suffered astronomical losses from a cyberattack believed to have been carried out by a hacking group," President Lee Jae-myung said.
"As hacking techniques become increasingly intelligent, sophisticated and commonplace with the development of artificial intelligence, existing security systems centred on inspections and responses after incidents have revealed clear limitations," he said.
The logo for cryptocurrency site Binance on a mobile phone in New York, 31 January, 2023AP Photo
"We must establish a comprehensive prevention system to address the cybersecurity crisis," he added.
Monday's launch by North Korea involved strategic cruise missiles fitted with a new cluster-munition warhead, the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported on Tuesday.
"The middle-sized dispersal warhead tipped on the cruise missile is capable of turning into ashes a target area of 5 to 6 hectares with its highest-density power," KCNA said.
KCNA said the test had "perfected the capability to deliver a vertical strike against the target by improving the terminal manoeuvrability of the cruise missile".
New launch vehicles for nuclear-capable short-range missiles during a military ceremony in Pyongyang, 18 February, 2026AP Photo
A North Korean official was quoted as saying the test was conducted "because our armed forces should defend the security of the country and deter all sorts of threats."
North Korea is demonstrating that they are capable of disabling "key South Korean and US military infrastructure, including airfield runways, radar bases, air defence batteries and assembled troops, with a single cruise missile", Lim Eul-chul, a professor at the Institute for Far Eastern Studies at Kyungnam University, told AFP.
The launch also aims to provide a "double deterrence against South Korea by strengthening conventional asymmetric strike capabilities at a stage before the use of nuclear weapons", he said.
The nuclear-armed North recently trialled a range of weaponry including attack drones, a new precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.
South Korea's military did not announce the cruise missile launch, as it had also not done with Sunday's test.

Unlike ballistic missile launches, North Korean cruise missile tests are not prohibited by UN Security Council sanctions.
Asked on Monday about Sunday's reported test, Joint Chiefs of Staff spokesperson Jang Do-young said South Korea and the United States were "closely coordinating and conducting a highly detailed analysis of its characteristics and specifications".
"Our military does not announce all projectiles launched by North Korea," Jang said, citing operational security and the protection of intelligence assets.

North Korea rejected allegations linking Pyongyang to theestimated$6.3 billionBinancehack, calling the accusation a “grave political provocation,” according to state media.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denounced the FBI's attribution of the attack to North Korea-linked hacking group TraderTraitor, YohnapreportedTuesday, citing the state-run Korean Central News Agency.
Blockchain analytics firms including Elliptic and Chainalysis have also linked the attack and subsequent movement of the stolen funds to North Korea-linked actors.
"The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a 'cyber criminal state', claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organization 'supported' by the DPRK was involved in the incident," Kim said, according to KCNA.
She accused Washington of misleading international public opinion by portraying cybercrimes around the world as the work of North Korea.
Separately, BinancesaidTuesday it would begin progressively reopening withdrawals for additional crypto assets across more networks, expanding its phased restoration of services following last week's hack.
The denial comes as blockchain analytics firms trace billions of dollars in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance through thousands of wallets across multiple blockchains.
Elliptic andChainalysissaid hackers linked to North Korea have used increasingly complex techniques to obscure the trail of the funds.
In the first four days after the attack, the hackers used roughly 12,000 wallets across 11 blockchains and conducted more than 40,000 transactions, Ellipticsaid in a reportMonday. The activity appeared highly complex and automated, with an average of one new wallet used every 25 seconds.
Much of the laundering activity initially took place on the Tron blockchain, where stolen funds were distributed across about 7,700 addresses before being moved to Ethereum through cross-chain bridges, according to Elliptic. At least $147 million had been transferred out of Tron through such bridges.
The hackers also used decentralized exchanges to swap stolen stablecoins into cryptocurrencies that cannot be frozen by their issuers, including ether. Elliptic said roughly $786 million in stablecoins was converted before issuers including Tether and Circle froze the remaining assets.
The laundering operation has since expanded to other blockchains, includingSolana. ChainalysissaidNorth Korea-linked actors had begun a new phase of laundering after moving more than $500 million through intermediary wallets on Tron.
Elliptic also identified the first signs of bitcoin mixing, a technique designed to make transactions harder to trace. About 28 bitcoin, worth $2.2 million, had passed through 18 mixing transactions as of early Monday, the firm said.
Despite the extensive movement of funds, about $2.85 billion — or 44% of exactly $6.43 billion stolen as reported by Elliptic — has been frozen or seized, while roughly $3.24 billion remains in addresses linked to the theft, mostly in bitcoin and ether.
The firm said only a negligible amount of stolen funds appeared to have been cashed out, with most of the activity involving transfers or conversions between cryptocurrencies rather than exchanges into spendable funds.
Elliptic said the laundering has moved slower than after the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, when North Korean hackers moved all the stolen ether within 10 days. It expects the remaining funds to be gradually converted into bitcoin and potentially cashed out through over-the-counter brokers and exchanges over several months.
Binanceaddedit has covered about 95% of the affected amount, with the remaining 5% consisting of less liquid tokens that take longer to source. The exchange said it was working with industry partners to acquire the remaining assets.

In the first phase people holding the ethereum, USDT and USDC tokens on the ethereum blockchain were able to withdraw their funds, as well as some others held on the BNB Smart Chain blockchain. Later on Sunday, dealing in the Dogecoin and Avalanche currencies resumed on their own platforms.
The platform said it had replenished 90% of the ⁠amount stolen. The remaining 10% of tokens were less liquid, meaning they ⁠may take ​longer to buy, the company said in a post on X on Saturday.
Richard Teng, Binance’s co-chief executive, said separately that the company was “committed to covering the ⁠remaining 10%” and users would not bear the financial impact of the hack.

It came as the FBI on Saturday confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack.
TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused ofhacking into Sony Picturesas revenge for The Interview, a film that mocked the North Korean leader Kim Jong-un.

The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralised finance and instant swap services.

Teng said on Friday that the breach was a “complex attack” involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it ‌harder to trace and investigate.
Binance said it had set aside about $6.34bn of company funds to cover the losses. “Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026. The FBI refers to this specific North Korean malicious cyber activity as “TraderTraitor.”
The FBI, together with partners at the USSS and IRS-CI, has observed TraderTraitor actors converting stolen assets primarily into Ethereum (ETH). It is expected these assets will then be further laundered by converting them using DeFi and instant swap services as they prepare them for further laundering stages.
As expected, Binancereopened customer withdrawalstoday afterfreezing themin the immediate aftermath of the hack.

fact_units.text: North Korea slams FBI claims it was behind €5bn Binance hack and test fires missiles | Euronews
ByGavin BlackburnPublished on3 November 2026 - 7:53 GMT+1•Updated8:36ShareCommentsAdd Euronews on GoogleShareFacebookTwitterFlipboardSendRedditLinkedinMessengerTelegramVKBlueskyThreadsWhatsapp
A 2024 United Nations report said proceeds from North Korean cyberattacks had "reportedly helped to fund the country's development of weapons of mass destruction".

Pyongyang has blasted the FBI's allegations that it was behind the theft of $6 billion (€5.3 billion) from cryptocurrency platform Binance, as it test-fired strategic cruise missiles in a new display of its weapons capabilities.
The missile launch came on the heels of a public rebuttal from Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong-un, who slammed the FBI's allegations as a "grave political provocation".
On Saturday, theFBI said a North Korea-affiliated hacking group called TraderTraitorhad been behind the hack.

Experts see the incident as potentially the largest cryptocurrency theft in history, with a haul equalling "nearly a quarter of the DPRK's estimated annual GDP," Michael Bosack, founding director of the Parley Policy Institute and a former UN Command official, told the AFP news agency.
Kim Yo-jong said the FBI's claim was "absurd rhetoric and nothing new," given prior US allegations that Pyongyang was behind last year's major hack of Bybit.
Still, North Korea likely felt compelled to respond because of the "level of international attention on the incident", Bosack said.
A TV screen shows a file image of Kim Yo-jong during a news programme at the Seoul Railway Station in Seoul, 1 June, 2023AP Photo
The denial was aimed at maintaining channels through which North Korea could continue laundering and using the cryptocurrency, Bosack added.
"If external parties start closing doors based on the international heat on the matter, then the stolen cryptocurrency does nothing to support the Kim regime's near-term priorities," he said.
The hack has prompted South Korea to call for increased protections for its digital infrastructure against cyberattacks.
"Not long ago, even the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange suffered astronomical losses from a cyberattack believed to have been carried out by a hacking group," President Lee Jae-myung said.

"As hacking techniques become increasingly intelligent, sophisticated and commonplace with the development of artificial intelligence, existing security systems centred on inspections and responses after incidents have revealed clear limitations," he said.
The logo for cryptocurrency site Binance on a mobile phone in New York, 31 January, 2023AP Photo
"We must establish a comprehensive prevention system to address the cybersecurity crisis," he added.
Monday's launch by North Korea involved strategic cruise missiles fitted with a new cluster-munition warhead, the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported on Tuesday.
"The middle-sized dispersal warhead tipped on the cruise missile is capable of turning into ashes a target area of 5 to 6 hectares with its highest-density power," KCNA said.
KCNA said the test had "perfected the capability to deliver a vertical strike against the target by improving the terminal manoeuvrability of the cruise missile".
New launch vehicles for nuclear-capable short-range missiles during a military ceremony in Pyongyang, 18 February, 2026AP Photo
A North Korean official was quoted as saying the test was conducted "because our armed forces should defend the security of the country and deter all sorts of threats."

North Korea is demonstrating that they are capable of disabling "key South Korean and US military infrastructure, including airfield runways, radar bases, air defence batteries and assembled troops, with a single cruise missile", Lim Eul-chul, a professor at the Institute for Far Eastern Studies at Kyungnam University, told AFP.
The launch also aims to provide a "double deterrence against South Korea by strengthening conventional asymmetric strike capabilities at a stage before the use of nuclear weapons", he said.
The nuclear-armed North recently trialled a range of weaponry including attack drones, a new precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.
South Korea's military did not announce the cruise missile launch, as it had also not done with Sunday's test.

Unlike ballistic missile launches, North Korean cruise missile tests are not prohibited by UN Security Council sanctions.

Asked on Monday about Sunday's reported test, Joint Chiefs of Staff spokesperson Jang Do-young said South Korea and the United States were "closely coordinating and conducting a highly detailed analysis of its characteristics and specifications".
"Our military does not announce all projectiles launched by North Korea," Jang said, citing operational security and the protection of intelligence assets.

Đội từng thua Việt Nam bị truy tố tội 'tự làm suy yếu chính mình' - Tuổi Trẻ OnlineBỏ qua đến nội dung chính

Đội từng thua Việt Nam bị truy tố tội 'tự làm suy yếu chính mình'
Cuối tuần rồi, bốn quan chức cấp cao của bóng đá Nepal, trong đó có chủ tịch liên đoàn, bị truy tố vì nghi thông đồng khiến đội tuyển quốc gia mất lợi thế sân nhà ở vòng loại World Cup 2026.
Nepal (áo đỏ) từng đối đầu Việt Nam trên sân Thống Nhất, trong trận đấu được tính là sân nhà của họ - Ảnh: NGUYÊN KHÔI
Theo báoOnlineKhabar,cơ quancông tố quận Lalitpur (Nepal) đã truy tố bốn quan chức Liên đoàn Bóng đá Nepal (ANFA), gồm Chủ tịch Pankaj Bikram Nembang, Tổng thư ký Kiran Rai, thủ quỹ Rabindra Joshi và nhân viên kế toán Sanjiv Pandey.
Đáng chú ý, Nepal cũng là đội tuyển từng hai lần thất bại trước Việt Nam tại vòng loại Asian Cup 2027.
Bị truy tố tội danh "làm suy yếu đội tuyển quốc gia"
Các cáo buộc liên quan trực tiếp đến gian lậntài chínhvà hành vi "thông đồng gây bất lợi cho chính đội tuyển Nepal" ở vòng loại World Cup 2026.
Đáng chú ý, những người đứng đầu ANFA bị nghi đã góp phần khiến đội nhà không thể tổ chức trận đấu trên sân nhà, đồng thời tạo điều kiện cho đối thủ hưởng lợi.
Câu chuyện bắt đầu từ tháng 3-2024, khi Nepal dự kiến tiếp Bahrain trên sân Dasharath ở Kathmandu trong khuôn khổ vòng loại thứ hai World Cup 2026.
Tuy nhiên, Liên đoàn Bóng đá châu Á (AFC) xác định sân Dasharath không đáp ứng điều kiện thi đấu quốc tế vì mặt cỏ xuống cấp nghiêm trọng.
Con trai Ronaldo đạt cột mốc sự nghiệp quan trọngĐỌC NGAY
Nepal buộc phải chuyển trận đấu ra nước ngoài. Điều bất thường là thay vì lựa chọn một sân trung lập tại quốc gia thứ ba, ANFA lại đồng ý đưa trận đấu sang Bahrain, tức sân nhà của chính đối thủ.
Kết quả, Nepal thảm bại 0-5 ngày 21-3-2024, rồi tiếp tục thua 0-3 trong trận lượt về năm ngày sau đó. Cả hai trận đều diễn ra trên đất Bahrain.
Theo kết quả điều tra của Cục Điều tra trung ương Nepal (CIB), lãnh đạo ANFA bị nghi đã góp phần khiến sân Dasharath không đủ điều kiện thi đấu.
Cụ thể, trong khoảng năm tháng từ trận gặp Yemen đến trận Bahrain, sân Dasharath liên tục được sử dụng để tổ chức các sự kiện khác, khiến mặt cỏ xuống cấp mà không được khắc phục kịp thời.
CIB còn phát hiện Chủ tịch Nembang và Tổng thư ký Rai không gặp giám sát viên AFC Mindu Dorji khi ông đến kiểm tra sân.
Ông Nembang, nhân vật trung tâm vụ án - Ảnh: GOAL NEPAL
Đặc biệt, ngày 4-3-2024, ông Rai đã ký thỏa thuận chuyển trận đấu sang Bahrain, trước bốn ngày so với văn bản AFC chính thức yêu cầu Nepal đề xuất sân trung lập.
Theo cơ quan điều tra, việc ký kết không được Ban chấp hành ANFA phê chuẩn, cũng không thông báo cho Bộ Thanh niên và Thể thao cùng Hội đồng Thể thao quốc gia Nepal.
CIB nghi ngờ các quan chức đã thông đồng với phía đối thủ, gây bất lợi cho Nepal và giúp Bahrain hưởng lợi.
Tuy nhiên, sân Dasharath thuộc quyền quản lý hạ tầng của Hội đồng Thể thao quốc gia. Trách nhiệm khiến sân xuống cấp từng là vấn đề tranh cãi giữa cơ quan này và ANFA. Hiện chưa có phán quyết xác định lãnh đạo liên đoàn cố tình phá hoại mặt sân hay dàn xếp kết quả thi đấu.
Cũng gặp bất lợi khi đá sân nhà với Việt Nam
Ngoài nghi vấn liên quan trận Bahrain, cuộc điều tra còn phát hiện những bất thường tài chính.
Theo CIB, thỏa thuận giữa ANFA và Liên đoàn Bóng đá Bahrain quy định phía Bahrain phải chuyển 20.000 USD tiền doanh thu bán vé cho Nepal. Tuy nhiên, khoản tiền này không xuất hiện trong tài khoản chính thức của ANFA.
Cơ quan điều tra còn nêu nghi vấn gian lận mua sắm trang thiết bị thể thao, khi ba doanh nghiệp tham gia chào giá được xác định có cùng chủ sở hữu.
Việc phân phối 330 vé World Cup 2026 do FIFA cấp cho ANFA cũng bị điều tra vì thiếu minh bạch về người mua và giá bán. Cơ quan công tố yêu cầu bốn bị cáo bồi hoàn tổng cộng hơn 9,3 triệu rupee Nepal.
Nepal (áo đỏ) trong trận gặp Bahrain ở vòng loại World Cup 2026 - Ảnh: AFC
Ngày 28-10, Chủ tịch Nembang và Tổng thư ký Rai xuất hiện tại Tòa án quận Lalitpur để lấy lời khai, sau thời gian bị liệt vào diện bị cáo chưa trình diện.
Thẩm phán Hari Singh Dhami quyết định cho cả hai tại ngoại với mức bảo lãnh 500.000 rupee Nepal mỗi người.
Trước đó, thủ quỹ Joshi và nhân viên kế toán Pandey cũng được tại ngoại, với mức bảo lãnh lần lượt 1,5 triệu và 1,2 triệu rupee.
Ngày 31-10, nhóm thành viên chiếm đa số trong Ban chấp hành ANFA, do Phó chủ tịch cấp cao Bir Bahadur Khadka dẫn đầu, quyết định yêu cầu cả bốn quan chức giải trình về công tác quản lý và những sai phạm bị cáo buộc.
Đáng chú ý, Nepal từng thua Việt Nam 1-3 và 0-1 tại vòng loại Asian Cup 2027vào tháng 10-2025. Khi đó, đội tuyển Nepal cũng phải chuyển trận đấu mang danh nghĩa sân nhà sang sân Thống Nhất (TP.HCM), giúp Việt Nam được thi đấu cả hai lượt trận trên lãnh thổ của mình.
Tuy nhiên, nguyên nhân chuyển sân lần này là tình hình bất ổn tại Nepal. Chưa có bằng chứng cho thấy trận gặp Việt Nam liên quan đến các sai phạm đang bị điều tra.
Bóng đá Nepal còn rơi vào khủng hoảng khi ANFA bị FIFA đình chỉ từ tháng 6-2026 do sự can thiệp từ bên thứ ba vào hoạt động liên đoàn. Đây là vụ việc riêng, không phải án phạt liên quan nghi vấn thông đồng trong trận gặp Bahrain.
Trung Quốc giáng 'đòn trừng phạt' thứ 2 với Mbappe, nặng hơn đòn đầu
Không dừng lại ở việc cắt hợp đồng với Kylian Mbappe, làn sóng tẩy chay tại Trung Quốc đang lan sang cả những thương hiệu quốc tế hợp tác với siêu sao người Pháp, đẩy anh vào cuộc khủng hoảng thương mại ngày càng phức tạp.

Nhằm nâng tầm trải nghiệm tham gia bảo hiểm cho khách hàng,Công ty Bảo hiểm nhân thọ Prudentialkhông ngừng đẩy mạnh số hóa các dịch vụ chăm sóc khách hàng. Nếu trước đây, khách hàng cần gặp trực tiếp tư vấn viên hoặc đến quầy giao dịch để thực hiện các thủ tục liên quan đến hợp đồng bảo hiểm, thì quy trình hiện nay đã được chuyển đổi lên nền tảng số, giúp khách hàng chủ động thao tác mọi lúc, mọi nơi.
PRUOnline - quản lý hợp đồng trực tuyến: PRUOnline cho phép khách hàng tra cứu thông tin hợp đồng, thanh toán phí bảo hiểm và theo dõi quyền lợi trực tuyến trên điện thoại hoặc máy tính. Hệ thống này giúp người dùng quản lý hợp đồng linh hoạt hơn và dễ dàng
Giao dịch qua Zalo: Trang Zalo Official Account của Prudential tích hợp các tính năng như cập nhật thông tin về hợp đồng bảo hiểm, nộp phí bảo hiểm trực tuyến, gửi và theo dõi yêu cầu giải quyết quyền lợi bảo hiểm… Việc tích hợp các dịch vụ bảo hiểm vào nền tảng phổ biến giúp khách hàng thực hiện giao dịch thuận tiện.
Ứng dụng công nghệ vào quy trình thẩm định và chi trả
Tháng 11/2024, Prudential ứng dụng công nghệ nhận dạng ký tự quang học thế hệ mới (OCR - Optical Character Recognition) vào quy trình thẩm định và xét duyệt hồ sơ yêu cầu giải quyết quyền lợi bảo hiểm trực tuyến.
Với tốc độ xử lý nhanh và khả năng nhận dạng, trích xuất thông tin từ hình ảnh sang văn bản chính xác đến 96%, công nghệ OCR giúp hệ thống phản hồi gần như tức thì về tính hợp lệ của chứng từ và đẩy nhanh quy trình đưa ra quyết định xét duyệt hồ sơ.
Công nghệ OCR giúp quy trình chi trả chỉ còn tính bằng phút, mọi thủ tục trở nên nhanh chóng hơn (Ảnh: Prudential).
Việc triển khai chăm sóc khách hàng trên nền tảng số và công nghệ OCR hỗ trợ rút ngắn thời gian xử lý hợp đồng, đồng thời cho phép khách hàng chủ động theo dõi và quản lý quyền lợi bảo hiểm.
Những thay đổi này phản ánh xu hướng chung của ngành bảo hiểm trong việc áp dụng công nghệ để nâng cao hiệu quả vận hành và giảm thiểu thủ tục trực tiếp, tạo điều kiện để khách hàng thực hiện các giao dịch thuận tiện hơn.
Thiết kế giải pháp bảo hiểm phù hợp nhu cầu, phù hợp từng giai đoạn cuộc sống
Bên cạnh chuyển đổi số, Prudential cũng chú trọng phát triểndanh mục sản phẩm bảo hiểm nhân thọđa dạng, phù hợp với nhu cầu tài chính và sức khỏe của khách hàng ở từng giai đoạn khác nhau.
Đơn cử như sản phẩm bảo hiểm liên kết chung PRUBảo Vệ Tối Đa 2.0, giải pháp hoạch định tài chính trọn đời với quyền lợi bảo hiểm được tối ưu hóa theo khả năng tài chính của từng cá nhân.
PRUBảo Vệ Tối Đa 2.0 cung cấp 2 lựa chọn kế hoạch bảo hiểm gồm “Kế hoạch bảo hiểm cơ bản” để cân bằng quyền lợi bảo vệ và tích lũy hoặc “Kế hoạch bảo hiểm nâng cao” giúp tối ưu quyền lợi bảo vệ tài chính.
Sản phẩm còn có thể kết hợp với các sản phẩm bảo hiểm bán cùng đa dạng, cho người tham gia và gia đình vững tâm trước các rủi ro như tai nạn, bệnh lý nghiêm trọng, chăm sóc sức khỏe… Người tham gia có thể lựa chọn thêm các sản phẩm bảo hiểm bán cùng để mở rộng phạm vi bảo vệ cho bản thân và gia đình, đáp ứng nhu cầu chăm sóc sức khỏe, bệnh lý nghiêm trọng, tử vong, tai nạn, thương tật.
Ngoài ra, PRUBảo Vệ Tối Đa 2.0 còn được tích hợp quyền lợi thưởng và các quyền linh hoạt. Những quyền lợi này góp phần giúp người tham gia tích lũy tài sản bền vững theo thời gian và chủ động điều chỉnh kế hoạch tài chính theo từng giai đoạn cuộc đời.
PRUBảo Vệ Tối Đa 2.0 - giải pháp bảo vệ tối ưu và hỗ trợ tích lũy bền vững (Ảnh: Prudential).
Prudential Việt Nam đang áp dụng công nghệ vào nhiều khâu quản lý hợp đồng và dịch vụ khách hàng, từ chăm sóc trực tuyến đến thẩm định và chi trả quyền lợi. Các giải pháp bảo hiểm cũng được thiết kế linh hoạt để phù hợp với nhu cầu khác nhau của khách hàng. Những sự thay đổi này nhằm mục tiêu cải thiện hiệu quả quản lý và trải nghiệm dịch vụ, phù hợp với xu hướng số hóa trong ngành bảo hiểm hiện nay.

fact_units.text: Đội từng thua Việt Nam bị truy tố tội 'tự làm suy yếu chính mình' - Tuổi Trẻ OnlineBỏ qua đến nội dung chính
Đăng ký Tuổi Trẻ SaoVào trang Tuổi Trẻ Sao
Đội từng thua Việt Nam bị truy tố tội 'tự làm suy yếu chính mình'
Cuối tuần rồi, bốn quan chức cấp cao của bóng đá Nepal, trong đó có chủ tịch liên đoàn, bị truy tố vì nghi thông đồng khiến đội tuyển quốc gia mất lợi thế sân nhà ở vòng loại World Cup 2026.
Nepal (áo đỏ) từng đối đầu Việt Nam trên sân Thống Nhất, trong trận đấu được tính là sân nhà của họ - Ảnh: NGUYÊN KHÔI

Theo báoOnlineKhabar,cơ quancông tố quận Lalitpur (Nepal) đã truy tố bốn quan chức Liên đoàn Bóng đá Nepal (ANFA), gồm Chủ tịch Pankaj Bikram Nembang, Tổng thư ký Kiran Rai, thủ quỹ Rabindra Joshi và nhân viên kế toán Sanjiv Pandey.
Đáng chú ý, Nepal cũng là đội tuyển từng hai lần thất bại trước Việt Nam tại vòng loại Asian Cup 2027.
Bị truy tố tội danh "làm suy yếu đội tuyển quốc gia"
Các cáo buộc liên quan trực tiếp đến gian lậntài chínhvà hành vi "thông đồng gây bất lợi cho chính đội tuyển Nepal" ở vòng loại World Cup 2026.
Đáng chú ý, những người đứng đầu ANFA bị nghi đã góp phần khiến đội nhà không thể tổ chức trận đấu trên sân nhà, đồng thời tạo điều kiện cho đối thủ hưởng lợi.
Câu chuyện bắt đầu từ tháng 3-2024, khi Nepal dự kiến tiếp Bahrain trên sân Dasharath ở Kathmandu trong khuôn khổ vòng loại thứ hai World Cup 2026.
Tuy nhiên, Liên đoàn Bóng đá châu Á (AFC) xác định sân Dasharath không đáp ứng điều kiện thi đấu quốc tế vì mặt cỏ xuống cấp nghiêm trọng.
Con trai Ronaldo đạt cột mốc sự nghiệp quan trọngĐỌC NGAY
Nepal buộc phải chuyển trận đấu ra nước ngoài.
Điều bất thường là thay vì lựa chọn một sân trung lập tại quốc gia thứ ba, ANFA lại đồng ý đưa trận đấu sang Bahrain, tức sân nhà của chính đối thủ.
Kết quả, Nepal thảm bại 0-5 ngày 21-3-2024, rồi tiếp tục thua 0-3 trong trận lượt về năm ngày sau đó.
Cả hai trận đều diễn ra trên đất Bahrain.
Theo kết quả điều tra của Cục Điều tra trung ương Nepal (CIB), lãnh đạo ANFA bị nghi đã góp phần khiến sân Dasharath không đủ điều kiện thi đấu.
Cụ thể, trong khoảng năm tháng từ trận gặp Yemen đến trận Bahrain, sân Dasharath liên tục được sử dụng để tổ chức các sự kiện khác, khiến mặt cỏ xuống cấp mà không được khắc phục kịp thời.
CIB còn phát hiện Chủ tịch Nembang và Tổng thư ký Rai không gặp giám sát viên AFC Mindu Dorji khi ông đến kiểm tra sân.
Ông Nembang, nhân vật trung tâm vụ án - Ảnh: GOAL NEPAL
Đặc biệt, ngày 4-3-2024, ông Rai đã ký thỏa thuận chuyển trận đấu sang Bahrain, trước bốn ngày so với văn bản AFC chính thức yêu cầu Nepal đề xuất sân trung lập.
Theo cơ quan điều tra, việc ký kết không được Ban chấp hành ANFA phê chuẩn, cũng không thông báo cho Bộ Thanh niên và Thể thao cùng Hội đồng Thể thao quốc gia Nepal.
CIB nghi ngờ các quan chức đã thông đồng với phía đối thủ, gây bất lợi cho Nepal và giúp Bahrain hưởng lợi.
Tuy nhiên, sân Dasharath thuộc quyền quản lý hạ tầng của Hội đồng Thể thao quốc gia.
Trách nhiệm khiến sân xuống cấp từng là vấn đề tranh cãi giữa cơ quan này và ANFA.
Hiện chưa có phán quyết xác định lãnh đạo liên đoàn cố tình phá hoại mặt sân hay dàn xếp kết quả thi đấu.
Cũng gặp bất lợi khi đá sân nhà với Việt Nam
Ngoài nghi vấn liên quan trận Bahrain, cuộc điều tra còn phát hiện những bất thường tài chính.
Theo CIB, thỏa thuận giữa ANFA và Liên đoàn Bóng đá Bahrain quy định phía Bahrain phải chuyển 20.000 USD tiền doanh thu bán vé cho Nepal.
Tuy nhiên, khoản tiền này không xuất hiện trong tài khoản chính thức của ANFA.
Cơ quan điều tra còn nêu nghi vấn gian lận mua sắm trang thiết bị thể thao, khi ba doanh nghiệp tham gia chào giá được xác định có cùng chủ sở hữu.
Việc phân phối 330 vé World Cup 2026 do FIFA cấp cho ANFA cũng bị điều tra vì thiếu minh bạch về người mua và giá bán.
Cơ quan công tố yêu cầu bốn bị cáo bồi hoàn tổng cộng hơn 9,3 triệu rupee Nepal.
Nepal (áo đỏ) trong trận gặp Bahrain ở vòng loại World Cup 2026 - Ảnh: AFC
Ngày 28-10, Chủ tịch Nembang và Tổng thư ký Rai xuất hiện tại Tòa án quận Lalitpur để lấy lời khai, sau thời gian bị liệt vào diện bị cáo chưa trình diện.
Thẩm phán Hari Singh Dhami quyết định cho cả hai tại ngoại với mức bảo lãnh 500.000 rupee Nepal mỗi người.
Trước đó, thủ quỹ Joshi và nhân viên kế toán Pandey cũng được tại ngoại, với mức bảo lãnh lần lượt 1,5 triệu và 1,2 triệu rupee.

Ngày 31-10, nhóm thành viên chiếm đa số trong Ban chấp hành ANFA, do Phó chủ tịch cấp cao Bir Bahadur Khadka dẫn đầu, quyết định yêu cầu cả bốn quan chức giải trình về công tác quản lý và những sai phạm bị cáo buộc.
Đáng chú ý, Nepal từng thua Việt Nam 1-3 và 0-1 tại vòng loại Asian Cup 2027vào tháng 10-2025.

Đoàn đưa tang bị ong tấn công, 2 người nhập viện cấp cứu
Một đoàn đưa tang tại phường Nam Đông Hà (Quảng Trị) vừa bị ong tấn công khiến nhiều người bị đốt. Đến thời điểm hiện tại đã có 2 người phải nhập viện cấp cứu.
Ong bất ngờ tấn công đoàn người đưa tang khiến 2 người nhập viện - Ảnh: AI
Trưa 3-11, Bệnh viện Đa khoa tỉnh Quảng Trị xác nhận vừa tiếp nhận cấp cứu với 2 trường hợp bịong tấn công.
"Hiện chúng tôi đã thực hiện các biện pháp cấp cứu ban đầu. Hai trường hợp đều bị khá nhiều vết đốt của ong và có các triệu chứng đau nhức",bác sĩ bệnh viện này cho biết.
Theo các bác sĩ, các bệnh nhân mới nhập viện khoảng 1 giờ, nênphải cần theo dõi thêm nhiều thời gian để xác định các triệu chứng nguy hiểm khác như sốc phản vệ, suy thận...
2 trường hợp phải nhập viện là bà H.T.H.C. (42 tuổi, trú xã Hiếu Giang) và ông N.K.P. (60 tuổi, trú phường Đông Hà).
Các nạn nhân này cho biết sáng cùng ngày, khoảng vài chục người cùng tham gia một đoàn đưa tang đến nghĩa địa ở khu vực đồi núi thuộc phường Nam Đông Hà.
Cứu người phụ nữ 36 tuổi sốc phản vệ vì bị ong đốt
Bất ngờ, một đàn ong lao ra tấn công cả đoàn. Rất nhiều người đã bị ong đốt. Nhưng hiện mới chỉ có 2 người có triệu chứng nặng nhất được đưa đến bệnh viện.
Trước đó hơn 1 tuần cũng tại Quảng Trị, 27 học sinh của Trường THCSHải Lăngcũng đã phải nhập viện vì bị một tổ ong trên cây xà cừ giữa sân trường tấn công.
Rất may, không có em nào có các triệu chứng nặng. Sau khi điều trị và theo dõi, các em đều về nhà trong điều kiện sức khỏe ổn định.
Học sinh nghịch ném đá tổ ong trong sân trường, 27 em bị ong đốt nhập viện
Một nhóm học sinh lớp 6 thuộc Trường THCS Hải Lăng (tỉnh Quảng Trị) dùng đá ném vào tổ ong trên cây giữa sân trường. Đàn ong sau đó lao xuống tấn công khiến 27 học sinh nhập viện.

Trường trung cấp nghề Vạn Ninh về Bộ Công an quản lý, không gián đoạn đào tạo
Bá Duy- baduybtn@outlook.com03/11/2026 14:53 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!
Trường trung cấp nghề Vạn Ninh (Khánh Hòa) chính thức được chuyển giao nguyên trạng về Bộ Công an quản lý, với yêu cầu tổ chức bộ máy tinh gọn, hiệu quả và không làm gián đoạn việc đào tạo.
Ngày 3.11, lãnh đạo UBND tỉnh Khánh Hòa xác nhận đã nhận được quyết định do Phó thủ tướng Lê Tiến Châu ký ngày 2.11, chuyển giao nguyên trạng Trường trung cấp nghề Vạn Ninh từ UBND tỉnh Khánh Hòa vềBộ Công anquản lý. Quyết định có hiệu lực từ ngày ký.
Theo quyết định, UBND tỉnh Khánh Hòa thực hiện bàn giao nguyên trạng trường về Bộ Công an. Đồng thời, tỉnh chủ trì, phối hợp các bộ Công an, Nội vụ, Tài chính, GD-ĐT điều chuyển biên chế viên chức, người lao động, bàn giao tài chính, tài sản, trụ sở của trường để quản lý theo quy định.
Bộ Công an tiếp nhận nguyên trạng trường, phối hợp UBND tỉnh Khánh Hòa và các bộ liên quan hoàn tất việc điều chuyển nhân sự, tài chính, tài sản, trụ sở.
Sau khi tiếp nhận, Bộ Công an chỉ đạo trường sắp xếp tổ chức bộ máy, nhân sự, quy định chức năng, nhiệm vụ của các đơn vị thuộc và trực thuộc theo quy định của pháp luật và củaBộ Công an. Hoạt động của trường phải bảo đảm tinh gọn, hiệu lực, hiệu quả, không làm gián đoạn hoạt động đào tạo hiện nay.
Tập thể cán bộ Trường trung cấp nghề Vạn Ninh tại lễ khai giảng năm học 2026-2027
ẢNH: ĐOÀN TRƯỜNG TRUNG CẤP NGHỀ VẠN NINH
Việc chuyển giao được thực hiện theo đề nghị của UBND tỉnh Khánh Hòa. Thực hiện kết luận của Ban Bí thư về đề án đào tạo nghề và giới thiệu việc làm cho nhóm đối tượng đặc thù là công dân đã hoàn thành nghĩa vụ tham gia Công an nhân dân, người chấp hành xong án phạt tù tái hòa nhập cộng đồng, người đang cai nghiện tại cơ sở cai nghiện ma túy, UBND tỉnh Khánh Hòa đã tổ chức xây dựng đề án chuyển giao trường về Bộ Công an.
Theo UBND tỉnh, mục tiêu là phát huy năng lực đào tạo của cơ sở giáo dục nghề nghiệp công lập hiện có, gắn đào tạo nghề, hỗ trợ việc làm với bảo đảm an sinh xã hội và phòng ngừa xã hội.
Trước đó, ngày 28.7, Văn phòng Bộ Công an thông báo ý kiến của Bộ trưởng Bộ Công an đồng ý đề xuất của Công an tỉnhKhánh Hòavề việc tiếp nhận trường. Ngày 12.9, UBND tỉnh giao Công an tỉnh chủ trì, phối hợp các sở, ngành và nhà trường xây dựng đề án. Đoàn đưa tang bị ong tấn công, 2 người nhập viện cấp cứu
Một đoàn đưa tang tại phường Nam Đông Hà (Quảng Trị) vừa bị ong tấn công khiến nhiều người bị đốt.
Đến thời điểm hiện tại đã có 2 người phải nhập viện cấp cứu.
Ong bất ngờ tấn công đoàn người đưa tang khiến 2 người nhập viện - Ảnh: AI
Trưa 3-11, Bệnh viện Đa khoa tỉnh Quảng Trị xác nhận vừa tiếp nhận cấp cứu với 2 trường hợp bịong tấn công.
"Hiện chúng tôi đã thực hiện các biện pháp cấp cứu ban đầu.
Hai trường hợp đều bị khá nhiều vết đốt của ong và có các triệu chứng đau nhức",bác sĩ bệnh viện này cho biết.
Theo các bác sĩ, các bệnh nhân mới nhập viện khoảng 1 giờ, nênphải cần theo dõi thêm nhiều thời gian để xác định các triệu chứng nguy hiểm khác như sốc phản vệ, suy thận...
2 trường hợp phải nhập viện là bà H.T.H.C.
(42 tuổi, trú xã Hiếu Giang) và ông N.K.P.
(60 tuổi, trú phường Đông Hà).
Các nạn nhân này cho biết sáng cùng ngày, khoảng vài chục người cùng tham gia một đoàn đưa tang đến nghĩa địa ở khu vực đồi núi thuộc phường Nam Đông Hà.
Cứu người phụ nữ 36 tuổi sốc phản vệ vì bị ong đốt
Bất ngờ, một đàn ong lao ra tấn công cả đoàn.
Nhưng hiện mới chỉ có 2 người có triệu chứng nặng nhất được đưa đến bệnh viện.
Trước đó hơn 1 tuần cũng tại Quảng Trị, 27 học sinh của Trường THCSHải Lăngcũng đã phải nhập viện vì bị một tổ ong trên cây xà cừ giữa sân trường tấn công.
Rất may, không có em nào có các triệu chứng nặng.
Sau khi điều trị và theo dõi, các em đều về nhà trong điều kiện sức khỏe ổn định.
Học sinh nghịch ném đá tổ ong trong sân trường, 27 em bị ong đốt nhập viện
Một nhóm học sinh lớp 6 thuộc Trường THCS Hải Lăng (tỉnh Quảng Trị) dùng đá ném vào tổ ong trên cây giữa sân trường.
Đàn ong sau đó lao xuống tấn công khiến 27 học sinh nhập viện.

lead_title: Melbourne Cup 2026: King Charles’ former horse Point of Law storms home to win

evidence_pages.https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n:
Melbourne Cup 2026: King Charles’ former horse Point of Law storms home to win | Melbourne Cup | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Point of Law wins the 2026 Melbourne Cup as jockey Ethan Brown salutes ahead of Zahrann and Juja Kibo at Flemington Racecourse.Photograph: Josh Chadwick/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenPoint of Law wins the 2026 Melbourne Cup as jockey Ethan Brown salutes ahead of Zahrann and Juja Kibo at Flemington Racecourse.Photograph: Josh Chadwick/Getty Images
Melbourne Cup 2026: King Charles’ former horse Point of Law storms home to win
Jockey Ethan Brown salutes after chasing down Royal Supremacy
Winning trainer Ciaron Maher fills top three places at Flemington
Point of Law justified his favouritism at the 2026Melbourne Cupafter the three-year-old stallion that was owned by King Charles until earlier this year reeled in Royal Supremacy in a thrilling feature race at Flemington Racecourse.
Jockey Ethan Brown guided the Ciaron Maher-trained horse to victory in the $10m race after Royal Supremacy – another in Maher’s stable – had led by about 20 lengths at one point.
Guardian Essential poll: record number of Australians are turning their backs on the Melbourne CupRead more
Maher had a record seven horses in Tuesday’s race and became the first trainer to achieve the trifecta, with Zahrann coming in second and another from his stable, Juja Kibo, third. The Joseph O’Brien-trained Sons and Lovers finished fourth.
It is the second time Maher has overseen a winner in the “race that stops the nation”, while victory for Brown marked a stunning turnaround in his fortunes after he nearly died in a horrendous fall three years ago.
Point of Law was bought by an Australian syndicate from King Charles in August and surged to the top of the betting after a strong performance in the Geelong Cup.
View image in fullscreenEthan Brown rides Point Of Law to victory in the 2026 Melbourne Cup Day at Flemington Racecourse.Photograph: Quinn Rooney/Getty Images
“He’s going to be a superstar. Stunning horse this,” Brown told Channel Nine after his victory, adding that winning the Melbourne Cup was a dream come true.
“Please don’t wake me up,” he said. “It’s every jockey’s dream to do this. And I can’t believe it. I was confident in the horse. Everyone I’ve spoken to said they’ve never gone in with that confidence.
“He’s in such good hands with Ciaron. He had the best turn of foot in the race. I thought he ran really well and he’s going to be a future star if he’s not already one today.”
Brown spent six months out of the saddle after a serious fall in the 2023 Australian Guineas at Flemington that left him in hospital and considering his future in racing.
“There was something burning inside me,” Brown said. “I was inches from losing my life, but a bit of time off and I realised I wasn’t any good at anything else. There was a slow burn inside of me [to come back].”
Point of Law was purchased from the royal stable in the UK after winning the Group 3 Bahrain Trophy at Newmarket in July.
“I knew I had my best hand going into it, but we just had to execute,” Maher told Nine. “I certainly didn’t know that Royal Supremacy would lead by that far, but it is a true test of staying and, Point of Law, he’s just thrived.
“It has been a whirlwind but I’m very proud of all the team to get three horses in the first three spots.”
After pop star Robbie Williams had urged those massed at Flemington to “let me entertain you” and then delivered a typically uplifting pre-race performance, focus returned to the horses, with 23 of the expected 24 runners parading through the mounting yard.
View image in fullscreenRobbie Williams entertains the crowd on Melbourne Cup Day at Flemington Racecourse.Photograph: Martin Keep/AAP
Earlier, top trainer Chris Waller was fined $50,000 after his contender Asterix was scratched having been found to have received anti-inflammatory medication on race-day.
The application of Penetrene is generally allowed on horses but there is a blanket ban on race-day treatments. Waller revealed its use on the forelegs of Asterix, part-owned by former New Zealand cricketer Mark Greatbatch, hours before the race was a mistake.
“The horse gets the same treatment every day,” Waller said. “It’s a very basic liniment most stables use and I guess the pressure of race day, the person that looks after the horse, put it on his legs right in front of the security guard, nothing to hide.
“It’s not her fault, I’ve got to wear the responsibility, it’s my team. It’s rare for us to make mistakes but the pressure of race day, you can’t explain how it affects everybody, everyone is on edge on Melbourne Cup Day and you think a little bit differently.”
It left Hall of Fame trainer Waller with just one horse in the race, Soul of Spain, who finished 13th.

Melbourne Cup: King's former horse Point Of Law wins prestigious Australian race - BBC Sport
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Point of Law is going to be a "superstar", says jockey Ethan Brown
Point of Law, a horse previously owned by King Charles, snatched victory in a thrilling 166th staging of the Melbourne Cup.
The three-year-old colt, who was bought from the King for an undisclosed sum earlier this year, reeled in Royal Supremacy for a win on just his sixth career start.
Ridden by Australian jockey Ethan Brown, Point Of Law emerged from the middle of the pack and raced clear in the final 100m to finish ahead of Zahrann and Juja Kibo as Ciaron Maher became the first trainer to saddle the top three finishers.
The Melbourne Cup, run in Australia since 1861 is often referred to as the "race that stops a nation". With a prize of A$10.2m ($7.04m; £5.3m), it is the country's third richest race, but is considered the most prestigious.
"Don't wake me up, this is every jockey's dream," said a triumphant Brown.
He added that he was telling himself "just stay cool, stay patient" as Royal Supremacy raced more than a dozen lengths ahead, before pushing Point of Law to overtake on the home stretch.
The King sold Point of Law to a group of investors including former AFL player Chris Judd and his wife Bec.
"He's going to be a superstar horse. He's something special," said Brown of the horse that won the Geelong Cup last month. "He's in the best of hands with Ciaron Maher."
Maher had a record seven of the 23 horses in this year's cup.
Brown, who grew up in Alice Springs, said he never dreamed as a kid that he would be riding the Melbourne Cup, but he had been given "a lot of great support" in his career.
Brown was "inches from losing my life" after a fall from his horse in a 2023 race sent him to hospital and kept him out of racing for six months.
Tens of thousands of people enjoyed sunny weather at Flemington on Tuesday, where they were also entertained by Robbie Williams. Organisers said the UK pop star's appearance, which included a 10-piece band, dancers and pyrotechnics, was the biggest pre-cup performance ever staged at Flemington.
The day was not without controversy. One horse, Asterix, was scratched from the race earlier on Tuesday, after it was discovered a stable worker had administered it the medication penetrene earlier that morning.
The medication is used to treat inflammation and muscle soreness, but no treatments of any kind are permitted on race day. Race stewards said the medication was applied in error but still constituted a "serious breach", the Age reported. Trainer Chris Waller was reportedly fined A$50,000 (£26,000; $35,000) for what he described as a simple mistake by a staff member under pressure.
Outside Flemington, crowds from the Australia-wide "Nup to the Cup" movement also gathered to protest against horse racing on the industry's most high profile day. Some held signs with slogans including "horse racing kills", "don't bet on cruelty" and "no more whips".
Interest in the race among Australians has been declining, according to a Guardian Essential poll, which this year found just 9% of people said they had high interest in the race, and 23% had moderate interest. However more than 60% said it was a unique part of Australia's national identity.
Last year the Melbourne Cup drew a record $382.5 million in bets.

King Charles III showed off his dance moves during a colourful Junkanoo street parade in Nassau, the capital of the Bahamas, on Wednesday, 28 October, as part of his first Caribbean tour since becoming monarch.
TheBritish kingjoined in the celebrations,dancing to the rhythm of the traditional Junkanoo festivalbefore watching performers and decorated floats pass through the streets. Footage showsCharles dancing during the paradein an unusual moment of informality during theroyal visit to the Bahamas.
After the parade,Charles walked through Nassau's Parliament Square, stopping at market stalls tomeet local vendorsand examine handmade goods such as woven raffia baskets.
The king alsogreeted members of the publicwho gathered to see him.Junkanoois a longstanding Bahamian tradition celebrated through elaborate costumes, music, dancing and street processions.
The Bahamasgained independence from Britain in 1973butremains a Commonwealth realm with Charles III as its head of state. His visit brings together the country's cultural heritage and itscontinuing constitutional ties to the British monarchy.

Melbourne Cup 2026: King Charles’ former horse Point of Law storms home to win
Jockey Ethan Brown salutes after chasing down Royal Supremacy
Winning trainer Ciaron Maher fills top three places at Flemington

Point of Law justified his favouritism at the 2026Melbourne Cupafter the three-year-old stallion that was owned by King Charles until earlier this year reeled in Royal Supremacy in a thrilling feature race at Flemington Racecourse.
Jockey Ethan Brown guided the Ciaron Maher-trained horse to victory in the $10m race after Royal Supremacy – another in Maher’s stable – had led by about 20 lengths at one point.
Guardian Essential poll: record number of Australians are turning their backs on the Melbourne CupRead more
Maher had a record seven horses in Tuesday’s race and became the first trainer to achieve the trifecta, with Zahrann coming in second and another from his stable, Juja Kibo, third.

It is the second time Maher has overseen a winner in the “race that stops the nation”, while victory for Brown marked a stunning turnaround in his fortunes after he nearly died in a horrendous fall three years ago.
Point of Law was bought by an Australian syndicate from King Charles in August and surged to the top of the betting after a strong performance in the Geelong Cup.
View image in fullscreenEthan Brown rides Point Of Law to victory in the 2026 Melbourne Cup Day at Flemington Racecourse.Photograph: Quinn Rooney/Getty Images
Stunning horse this,” Brown told Channel Nine after his victory, adding that winning the Melbourne Cup was a dream come true.
Everyone I’ve spoken to said they’ve never gone in with that confidence.
He had the best turn of foot in the race.
I thought he ran really well and he’s going to be a future star if he’s not already one today.”
Brown spent six months out of the saddle after a serious fall in the 2023 Australian Guineas at Flemington that left him in hospital and considering his future in racing.
“I was inches from losing my life, but a bit of time off and I realised I wasn’t any good at anything else.
There was a slow burn inside of me [to come back].”
Point of Law was purchased from the royal stable in the UK after winning the Group 3 Bahrain Trophy at Newmarket in July.
“I knew I had my best hand going into it, but we just had to execute,” Maher told Nine.
“I certainly didn’t know that Royal Supremacy would lead by that far, but it is a true test of staying and, Point of Law, he’s just thrived.
“It has been a whirlwind but I’m very proud of all the team to get three horses in the first three spots.”

After pop star Robbie Williams had urged those massed at Flemington to “let me entertain you” and then delivered a typically uplifting pre-race performance, focus returned to the horses, with 23 of the expected 24 runners parading through the mounting yard.
View image in fullscreenRobbie Williams entertains the crowd on Melbourne Cup Day at Flemington Racecourse.Photograph: Martin Keep/AAP
Earlier, top trainer Chris Waller was fined $50,000 after his contender Asterix was scratched having been found to have received anti-inflammatory medication on race-day.
The application of Penetrene is generally allowed on horses but there is a blanket ban on race-day treatments.
Waller revealed its use on the forelegs of Asterix, part-owned by former New Zealand cricketer Mark Greatbatch, hours before the race was a mistake.
“The horse gets the same treatment every day,” Waller said.
“It’s a very basic liniment most stables use and I guess the pressure of race day, the person that looks after the horse, put it on his legs right in front of the security guard, nothing to hide.
“It’s not her fault, I’ve got to wear the responsibility, it’s my team.
It’s rare for us to make mistakes but the pressure of race day, you can’t explain how it affects everybody, everyone is on edge on Melbourne Cup Day and you think a little bit differently.”
It left Hall of Fame trainer Waller with just one horse in the race, Soul of Spain, who finished 13th.
Melbourne Cup: King's former horse Point Of Law wins prestigious Australian race - BBC Sport
Point of Law is going to be a "superstar", says jockey Ethan Brown
Point of Law, a horse previously owned by King Charles, snatched victory in a thrilling 166th staging of the Melbourne Cup.
The three-year-old colt, who was bought from the King for an undisclosed sum earlier this year, reeled in Royal Supremacy for a win on just his sixth career start.

Ridden by Australian jockey Ethan Brown, Point Of Law emerged from the middle of the pack and raced clear in the final 100m to finish ahead of Zahrann and Juja Kibo as Ciaron Maher became the first trainer to saddle the top three finishers.
The Melbourne Cup, run in Australia since 1861 is often referred to as the "race that stops a nation".
With a prize of A$10.2m ($7.04m; £5.3m), it is the country's third richest race, but is considered the most prestigious.
